title: SouthBay platform activation handshake
next_steps: Jordan to share onboarding runbook and pricing worksheet by 2027-01-05
Priya and Evan to schedule integration deep-dive and test plan week of 2027-01-10
Lena to open pilot project in CRM and send kickoff invite for pilot cadence
action_items: Jordan Meyers - Send onboarding runbook, sample config, and Dedicated vs Hosted cost matrix - 2027-01-05
Priya Raman - Prepare integration playbook and list of required IAM/Network artifacts for VPC peering - 2027-01-07
Evan Cho - Share VPN endpoint details and internal staging SSO test account - 2027-01-04
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-12-29 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Mark Delgado (CTO, SouthBay), Rina Patel (Head of ML), Evan Cho (Platform Lead), Sara Blum (VP Product)
summary: Kickoff handshake to align on activation scope for a pilot using Redwood's hosted API with option to move to Dedicated capacity. Discussed security/compliance needs (SSO, KMS, audit logs), integration touchpoints (VPC, peering, routing), success criteria, and immediate next steps to spin up a pilot environment and run smoke/latency tests.
topics: Owners and timeline for pilot artifacts
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Meyers: hey everyone thanks for joining on a tuesday afternoon, uh appreciate you carving out time. i'm jordan from redwood, i'll run the handshake today.
00:08 Mark Delgado: yeah thanks jordan, quick note from our side, we're on a tight timeline — board wants a pilot by mid feb, so hoping to get a runway.
00:16 Jordan Meyers: perfect, that helps. quick roll call? i saw rina, evan, sara — can you confirm?
00:22 Rina Patel: yep that's right, hey all.
00:23 Evan Cho: Evan here.
00:25 Sara Blum: Sara on product.
00:27 Priya Raman: priya from redwood se, i'll handle technical integration; happy to dig into network and auth.
00:33 Lena Ortiz: lena — customer success, i'll be your day-to-day contact for the activation.
00:37 Jordan Meyers: great. agenda — two parts: one, align on scope and success criteria; two, surface security/network blockers so we can list action items. does that work?
00:44 Mark Delgado: yes, and also a quick pricing sanity check, we need to know if cost will blow up with our high-throughput rerank jobs.
00:51 Jordan Meyers: sure, we'll cover batching and caching options that affect unit cost.
00:57 Priya Raman: to add — we'll suggest a small smoke test first: 2k requests/day with 256 token context to validate latency and token costs, then expand.
01:05 Rina Patel: that schedule sounds good. our main constraints: all PHI-ish data must not leave our VPC, we need KMS encryption and audit logs, and single sign-on via our Okta tenant.
01:18 Jordan Meyers: understood. quick clarifier — when you say PHI can't leave VPC, do you mean for pilot you prefer private deployment or are we allowed to route via hosted with encryption in transit?
01:28 Evan Cho: ideally we want private control plane but if hosted has strong encryption and guaranteed retention controls it could be acceptable for pilot.
01:36 Priya Raman: there's the middle ground — Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with VPC peering or Private deployment. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pool and VPC options; hosted is fastest to launch.
01:46 Mark Delgado: cost is a factor though; Dedicated commit is a bigger lift. can you show projected cost delta?
01:52 Jordan Meyers: yes i'll send a Dedicated vs Hosted cost matrix. quick note — we do prefix KV cache and batching that usually drops per-token cost 30-50% depending on request shape.
02:03 Sara Blum: can you explain the KV cache briefly? we had our data scientists ask what that means for personalization and context retention.
02:11 Priya Raman: sure — we call it kv cache, it's the mechanism for preserving key/value states across requests so repeated prefixes don't re-run full context. in practice it saves tokens for chat or rerank pipelines. sometimes folks call it "kv cash" in notes — small typo we see in transcripts.
02:25 Rina Patel: perfect. on SSO we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC support. you support SCIM?
02:32 Priya Raman: yes, SCIM provisioning is supported; SAML for login, SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC roles. we can share the SSO integration guide.
02:41 Evan Cho: network — we use AWS with strict egress controls. how do we do peering?
02:46 Priya Raman: we support VPC peering, PrivateLink in some regions, and VPN tunnels for on-prem. for AWS we typically request a VPC CIDR and a set of allowed IPs; we'll provide a template for peering and route tables.
02:59 Mark Delgado: any compliance attestations? SOC2 type II or iso?
03:03 Jordan Meyers: we have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO, plus detailed audit logs and optional log export to your SIEM. we'll attach those docs.
03:12 Sara Blum: good. about latency — our product target is 200-300ms p95 for generation for 256 tokens, can redwood meet that on hosted?
03:22 Priya Raman: typical hosted p95 for 256 tokens is in the 180-280ms range depending on model choice, and dedicated lowers variability. we can run a benchmark in your staging to validate.
03:34 Rina Patel: and what about model versioning? we want deterministic rollouts and canaries.
03:38 Jordan Meyers: rollouts are supported — you can pin model versions, do canary splits and automatic fallback to cheaper variants if errors spike.
03:46 Evan Cho: ok, what artifacts do you need from us to stand up pilot?
03:50 Priya Raman: we'll need: 1) account contacts and an Okta test tenant for SSO testing; 2) network details (VPC CIDR, peerable subnets, NAT info); 3) sample traffic shape and prompt examples; 4) a list of evaluation prompts for quality regression checks.
04:07 Evan Cho: i'll export that this week.
04:10 Mark Delgado: timeline — if we want pilot by mid feb, what are milestone dates?
04:14 Lena Ortiz: proposed runway: prep & access (2 weeks), integration & smoke tests (2 weeks), pilot ramp (4 weeks) = 8+ weeks. that maps to mid-feb if we start early january.
04:27 Jordan Meyers: noted. next — concerns about data retention. Do you want logs stored by us or pushed to your S3?
04:33 Rina Patel: prefer logs pushed to our encrypted S3 with lifecycle controls, but keep minimal retention on vendor side.
04:40 Priya Raman: we can export audit logs to your S3 and set vendor retention to a short window. we'll include the retention config options.
04:48 Sara Blum: what about rate limits? for rerank bursts we might see spikes.
04:52 Jordan Meyers: we have rate limiting quotas per account and token-based limits; dedicated includes configurable concurrency and burst capacity. we'll share suggested autoscale settings for your traffic profile.
05:03 Rina Patel: on legal — any data processing addendum or standard contractual clauses?
05:08 Jordan Meyers: yes DPA and SCCs available; our legal can start a redline. lena will coordinate.
05:14 Lena Ortiz: i'll kick that off after this call.
05:17 Mark Delgado: ok good. any blockers we haven't mentioned?
05:19 Evan Cho: small one — we use an internal model registry that expects a specific response schema; can redwood support structured outputs and tool/function calling?
05:29 Priya Raman: yes structured output and function calling supported; we also have schema validation hooks and can enforce response wrappers.
05:36 Sara Blum: sweet.
05:37 Jordan Meyers: recap and owners: jordan will send runbook and cost matrix; priya will send SSO and network playbook; evan will share staging creds and sample prompts; lena will open the pilot in crm and send invites. any timeline adjustments?
05:54 Mark Delgado: everyone's agreed — i'll expect the runbook by jan 5th and staging creds by jan 4th.
05:59 Jordan Meyers: perfect. final Qs?
06:02 Rina Patel: tiny nit — do you support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-kms)?
06:07 Priya Raman: yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have per-tenant managed keys with optional KMS integrations. we'll document the differences.
06:18 Sara Blum: ok that's all from product. thanks.
06:21 Jordan Meyers: thanks all. we'll follow up in email with docs and a calendar for the deep-dive.
06:27 Lena Ortiz: action items and next steps in the notes, i'll track.
06:30 Mark Delgado: thanks everyone.
06:33 [call ends]

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and filler words; Speaker labels may be approximate.
